pure-announcement.rationale: It is a vendor-flavoured explainer of the SARIF standard, not a launch note — the CodePathfinder promotion is wrapping around coverage of a durable interchange format.

duplicate.rationale: The nearest concept osv-format covers a vulnerability-database schema, not the static-analysis results interchange format; no existing concept covers SARIF.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The structural claims (runs/tool/results/rules, schema 2.1.0, GitHub Code Scanning ingestion) are checkable against the OASIS spec and GitHub docs.

durability.rationale: SARIF 2.1.0 is a stable OASIS standard consumed by GitHub Code Scanning since 2019, and the anatomy described (runs, tool.driver.rules, results with ruleId/message/locations) will hold in twelve months.

actionability.rationale: Standardising SAST output on SARIF to plug any scanner into code-scanning platforms is a real pipeline decision, and the schema anatomy given is enough to emit or parse the format beyond the CodePathfinder-specific steps.

atomicity.rationale: One idea — SARIF as the common interchange format for static-analysis findings — states in a paragraph; the CodePathfinder marketing is chaff, not a second concept.
